entries.summary: November 19, 2026 - The PostgreSQL Global Development Group today announced the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest version of the world's most advanced open source database.
entries.text: November 19, 2026 - The PostgreSQL Global Development Group today announced the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest version of the world's most advanced open source database. Mission-critical usage of PostgreSQL continues to rapidly rise, and PostgreSQL 19 responds to this by simplifying both administration and development for these workloads at scale. This release introduces the REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) command so users can optimize tables for their current workload without disruption to ongoing operations. PostgreSQL 19 gives users better control over plan stability and query performance with the new pg_plan_advice extension. Developers will find many delightful features in this release, from support for "read-your-writes" consistency on standbys to "get or create" behavior that saves a network round trip. "For over 30 years, the global open source community has built PostgreSQL into a database that organizations trust with their most critical data," said Jonathan Katz, a member of the PostgreSQL core team. "PostgreSQL 19 continues that commitment to reliability, giving users new ways to manage their workloads without disruption and to build applications that span multiple systems." PostgreSQL, an innovative data management system known for its reliability, robustness, and extensibility, benefits from 30 years of open source development from a global developer community and has become the preferred open source relational database for organizations of all sizes. entries.summary: The WAL-G team is pleased to announce the release of WAL-G 3.0.10. WAL-G is an open-source backup and recovery tool for PostgreSQL, Apache Cloudberry, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, and other databases.
entries.text: The WAL-G team is pleased to announce the release of WAL-G 3.0.10. WAL-G is an open-source backup and recovery tool for PostgreSQL, Apache Cloudberry, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, and other databases. The main new PostgreSQL feature is wal-send. It serves archived WAL over PostgreSQL's streaming replication protocol, allowing standbys and pg_receivewal to read WAL directly from object storage and follow new segments as they arrive. Other PostgreSQL improvements include: Continuous WAL archival in daemon mode: the pipeline keeps working between requests, and retained lookahead reduces directory scanning (#2697, #2698). Optional backup-push --wait-for-archive: WAL-G waits for all WAL segments required by the backup to reach the selected backup storage before publishing the backup as complete (#2722). Backup-name reservation before upload, protecting against concurrent reuse of the same name (#2707). WAL prefetch files are published only after a successful download (#2696), and WAL source files are closed after upload failures (#2695). Standard X/X LSN notation in catchup-push --from-lsn (#2643). S3 support now uses AWS SDK v2 and adds configurable request timeouts, retryable error codes, and checksum settings. Backup copying can use server-side S3 copy and configurable transfer concurrency. entries.summary: pgjumbo is a new desktop client for PostgreSQL 12+, free to use, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with query, data and administration tools.
entries.text: pgjumbo is a new desktop client for PostgreSQL 12+, free to use, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with query, data and administration tools. pgjumbo connects to PostgreSQL 12+, including Amazon Aurora and RDS with IAM authentication, directly, over SSL or through an SSH tunnel. Installers are available for Windows (x64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (AppImage, .deb and .rpm). Version 1.0.2 includes: An object explorer and inspector with each object's CREATE script, statistics and dependencies. A Query Tool with completion, syntax errors from PostgreSQL's own parser as you type, parameters, EXPLAIN as a table or a diagram, and results that can be sorted, filtered, compared and exported. A data editor that shows the statements before it saves them. Backup and restore built on pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore: choosing objects and rows, server backups as a folder of archives, reading an archive's contents before restoring, and restoring into a new database. Maintenance: what each table needs and what holds VACUUM back, VACUUM, ANALYZE and REINDEX as reviewed steps with progress, and autovacuum settings per table. Server activity, configuration, roles and privileges, logs, replication, pg_cron jobs and LISTEN/NOTIFY. Changes to objects are shown as SQL and reviewed before they run, and on servers marked Production, destructive statements ask for confirmation first. Download pgjumbo · Release notes for 1.0.2
entries.title: pgjumbo: a new free desktop client for PostgreSQL

entries.summary: CortexRidge has released pgSherpa, a free desktop companion for PostgreSQL on macOS, now available on the Mac App Store.
entries.text: CortexRidge has released pgSherpa, a free desktop companion for PostgreSQL on macOS, now available on the Mac App Store. pgSherpa sits in a corner of the screen and polls one or more PostgreSQL servers (PostgreSQL 12 to 18). When something needs attention it says so in a sentence, with the rows behind it: Health: lock-wait chains, long-running and idle-in-transaction sessions, replication lag and replication slots, vacuum and transaction ID wraparound, connection limits. Security: the server's version compared with the latest PostgreSQL minor release and the CVEs fixed since, plus configuration such as SSL, MD5 passwords and superuser count. Cloud: backups, failovers, maintenance windows and replicas for DigitalOcean Managed Databases, Supabase and Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL, read from the provider's API. SQL: a query box with PostgreSQL completion and \h syntax help for the server's own version. Every statement runs in a read-only transaction unless the user switches it to write. Reports: ready-made views of pg_stat_activity, pg_locks, pg_stat_statements, vacuum progress, indexes and replication. pgSherpa needs only a role with pg_monitor. It installs no extension and no agent on the server, and it has no account and no telemetry; passwords and keys stay in the macOS Keychain. It runs on macOS 12 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6833955115 More information: https://cortexridge.com/
entries.title: pgSherpa: a free PostgreSQL monitoring companion for macOS

entries.text: We are pleased to announce the release 1.1.1 of PG_CVE, a lightweight tool designed to provide DBAs and system administrators with a clear, up-to-date overview of CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), known exploits, and release stability across PostgreSQL versions. Key Features & Highlights: Rapid tracking of security advisories and CVEs associated with specific PostgreSQL versions. Overview of release stability and patch information to assist DBAs with upgrade planning. Security context: integration of known exploit data for accurate vulnerability triage. Lightweight, standalone web interface for fast client-side navigation. Links & Resources: Live Interactive Demo: https://meob.github.io/PG_CVE/?version=15.8 Source Code & Documentation: https://github.com/meob/PG_CVE

entries.summary: pg_fastload 1.0.0 is a parallel bulk loader for PostgreSQL, 1.58x faster than the best pg_bulkload mode and 6.07x faster than COPY.
entries.text: pg_fastload 1.0.0 is a parallel bulk loader for PostgreSQL, 1.58x faster than the best pg_bulkload mode and 6.07x faster than COPY. It parallelises the loading pipeline across background workers while keeping the load inside a single transaction. It is a source-level fork of pg_bulkload 3.1.23, so control-file syntax, TYPE values, log format and WRITER modes are unchanged. Repository: github.com/yuansong/pg_fastload Release: pg_fastload v1.0.0 License: BSD 3-Clause, with the upstream pg_bulkload copyright notices retained The problem pg_bulkload and COPY both run the whole load in one backend: read, parse, form the tuple, write. On a 16-core machine that leaves 15 cores idle, and the parse step is usually the expensive one. For CSV it is a byte-at-a-time state machine followed by a type input function per column. How it works The load has four stages: read input, parse record and split fields, form the tuple, and insert. Stages 1-3 move to background workers; stage 4 stays serial in the backend that issued the load: one reader worker -> N parser workers -> leader writes Design points that matter in practice: The input file is read exactly once. A single reader scans sequentially and hands chunks to the workers over shm_mq; the workers never open the file. Total read volume stays at 1x the file size, so the speedup does not invert once the data is larger than the page cache. It is still one transaction. entries.summary: The Apache Cloudberry (Incubating) community is pleased to announce the release of Apache Cloudberry 2.2.0, the latest version of its open-source massively parallel processing (MPP) database built on PostgreSQL for…
entries.text: The Apache Cloudberry (Incubating) community is pleased to announce the release of Apache Cloudberry 2.2.0, the latest version of its open-source massively parallel processing (MPP) database built on PostgreSQL for large-scale analytics and AI workloads. Following the 2.1.0 release, 2.2.0 continues the project's work on tracking upstream PostgreSQL, expanding the extension ecosystem, and broadening platform support. Key Enhancements in 2.2.0 Tracking upstream PostgreSQL: The kernel moves from PostgreSQL 14.4 to 14.10, absorbing upstream optimizations, fixes, and hardening one minor release at a time. Security fixes: Dozens of upstream PostgreSQL CVE fixes are included, along with targeted cherry-picks of advisories published after 14.10. Six new extensions: diskquota, gp_stats_collector, gp_relsizes_stats, reject_partition_fullscan, try_convert, and yezzey. Query processing and observability: Interconnect statistics views, intra-segment parallel table scan in the ORCA optimizer, parallel Hash Full Join and Right Join, and multi-table join support for answering queries using materialized views (AQUMV). Platform coverage: Rocky Linux 8, 9, and 10 and Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 are supported and tested in CI. Ubuntu 20.04 is no longer supported. Packaging: Automated DEB and RPM builds for x86_64 and ARM64, and relocatable RPMs that allow multiple Cloudberry major versions to coexist on the same host. entries.summary: Datasentinel 2026.10, the new release of our PostgreSQL monitoring and troubleshooting platform, is now available.
entries.text: Datasentinel 2026.10, the new release of our PostgreSQL monitoring and troubleshooting platform, is now available. It introduces AI Connector, which connects Datasentinel metrics to the AI assistant your team already uses. Ask a question in plain language, such as "why was the orders database slow at 9:00 this morning?". The assistant analyzes the collected data, explains what it finds and turns the evidence into concrete recommendations. AI Connector AI Connector works with the main AI assistants, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, and you choose the AI model behind them. It combines an MCP server, which gives the assistant access to Datasentinel metrics, with a Skill, which guides its analysis. It is an add-on, enabled by a licence option. What you can ask for: Past performance. Find out what happened on one instance or a group of instances, from slow queries to locks. Live troubleshooting. See what an instance is doing right now: running sessions, who is blocking whom, and how a query would be executed. Comparisons. Compare two periods, instances or applications, for example before and after a deployment. Recommendations. Get concrete advice on queries, indexes, settings and maintenance, based on your own metrics. Several ways to use it. The common way is to chat with your assistant, from a desktop app, a command line or an IDE. You can also generate dashboards on demand, for example as Claude artifacts, schedule health checks and digests

entries.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has released an update to all supported versions of PostgreSQL, including 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25, as well as the second release candidate of PostgreSQL 19.
entries.text: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has released an update to all supported versions of PostgreSQL, including 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25, as well as the second release candidate of PostgreSQL 19. This release fixes 52 security vulnerabilities and over 140 bugs reported over the last several months. There are several issues that may require you to take extra steps after updating, which are described in detail below. See the "Updating" section for more information on post-update steps you may need to take. For the full list of changes, please review the release notes. PostgreSQL 14 EOL Notice This is the final release of PostgreSQL 14. PostgreSQL 14 is now end-of-life and will no longer receive security and bug fixes. If you are running PostgreSQL 14 in a production environment, we suggest that you make plans to upgrade to a newer, supported version of PostgreSQL. Please see our versioning policy for more information. Security Issues The following security vulnerabilities are closed in this update release. You can find more details about the vulnerabilities and their affected versions in the links below: CVE-2026-6460: Type confusion after ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE executes arbitrary code (CVSS v3.1: 8.8) CVE-2026-6467: Extension script schema mishandling executes arbitrary SQL (CVSS v3.1: 7.2) CVE-2026-14661: dblink and subscriptions can append to arbitrary files (CVSS v3.1: 8.1) CVE-2026-16237: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read or modify rows despite auto-updatable
